cand.title: Gestion de projet – FER Genève session
cand.excerpt: Medium-high: exact dates, corporate audience and shared lunch; fixed venue lowers accessibility.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Frank Sobczak, Directeur, Département Formation, FER Genève: relevant senior training relationship contact, also officially listed for continuing education. Laurence Popovic, Chargée de projets, Département Formation, FER Genève: relevant operational routing contact, not verified as the manager of this particular course. Neither is evidenced as holding hotel/catering contract authority. Sylvain Grisard is the named course trainer and Responsable Distribution at G&F Châtelain, succursale de Chanel Sàrl; he should not be treated as the accommodation buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced upcoming session within the requested horizon: Tuesday 23 February, Wednesday 24 February and Tuesday 23 March 2027; each day 09:00–12:30 and 13:30–17:00. These are teaching dates, not publication dates. The first-to-last date span is not a continuous residential programme. No later edition through June 2028 was found officially announced.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment using the supplied hotel specification: low fit for the announced edition. The audience is managers, project leaders, business heads and HR leaders, which is compatible with a business-training product, but the class is already located in Plan-les-Ouates with shared lunch included. YOTEL Geneva Lake in Founex is outside that venue’s immediate territory. A future explicitly offsite workshop could suit its meeting product, subject to headcount, transport and verified catering capacity; no residential or resort requirement is evidenced. No basis exists to propose a 20–120-room block or the full hotel.
findings.venueCommitments: Published venue: Centre de formation FER Genève – SPARK, Chemin du Champ-des-Filles 4B / 4 entrée B, 1228 Plan-les-Ouates, canton of Geneva, Switzerland. Territory classification: elsewhere in Geneva canton, in the Geneva urban periphery; not Geneva city proper and not Founex/Nyon/La Côte/Geneva Airport corridor, Lausanne or French Pays de Gex. Venue is an education/conference facility, not a competing hotel. Publication confirms the announced venue, not the terms of an underlying contract.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified published editions: 3–4 April and 8 May 2025 at SPARK; 17–18 February and 17 March 2026 at SPARK; upcoming 23–24 February and 23 March 2027 at SPARK. The 2025 page explicitly says “CHANGEMENT DE LIEU” and names SPARK, but does not establish the superseded venue. Evidence supports repeated delivery at SPARK, not destination rotation, a guaranteed annual cycle or an announced 2028 edition.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. The 2027 page states “Repas de midi en commun inclus” and provides “T 058 715 33 15 E cours.seminaires@fer-ge.ch” for information. It publishes no lodging arrangements, housing bureau, host hotel, named hotel block, room inventory or accommodation RFP. No hotels are listed in the reviewed edition material. Included lunch is not evidence of an external catering tender. SPARK separately advertises “Une offre de restauration”, but that does not identify this course’s caterer or prove a catering contract.
findings.organizationStructure: FER Genève is an “Association patronale et économique”, not a PCO/DMC or corporate event agency. Its internal training department organizes continuing-education courses for company decision-makers. For this programme FER Genève is the organizer, SPARK the published training venue and Sylvain Grisard the trainer; no external housing intermediary or PCO is identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The evidenced incumbent is SPARK, not an incumbent hotel. Its published offering includes ten training rooms, an auditorium, technical assistance and catering. These are structural alternatives to moving the course into a hotel; they are not evidence of this course’s attendance or booked room size. No sold-out venue, overflow demand, hotel shortage, room block or room-night evidence was found.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Make one low-pressure qualification approach to Frank Sobczak via his published continuing-education contact, asking whether FER ever commissions external La Côte training days or needs accommodation for non-local trainers/participants. Ask him to route operational questions to the course coordinator; Laurence Popovic is a named departmental project contact, not an assumed course owner. Acknowledge SPARK and the included lunches; do not send an unsolicited displacement or room-block proposal. Advance only if an actual external sourcing requirement, headcount and decision-maker are confirmed.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Low and unproven: the 2027 course has a named SPARK venue and includes lunch. Do not mark hotel sourcing open or present the published course as an accessible Founex day-meeting/catering booking. Accommodation sourcing remains unconfirmed; any individual lodging enquiry would require a separately evidenced need. No delegate travel or Geneva Airport arrival evidence was found.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: limited, conditional relationship potential rather than a verified future hotel cycle. Repeated 2025–2027 delivery gives a legitimate reason to discuss future training formats, but repeated use of SPARK is a competitive constraint. An external La Côte workshop or residential module would need explicit organizer interest; neither a 2028 edition nor an external-venue procurement window is published.
